newsitem.title: USA: Texaco profits surge on court decision.
newsitem.headline: Texaco profits surge on court decision.

text.p: Texaco Inc Tuesday reported first quarter earnings of $980 million, or $3.72 per share, reflecting Monday's U.S. Supreme Court tax ruling in the company's favor.
The benefit from the tax decision was $488 million in the first quarter.
Net income before this benefit was $492 million, or $1.84 per share, ahead of analysts' forecasts of $1.72 and better than the year ago $1.42 per share.
The company said U.S. exploration and production earnings rose 16 percent to $311 million from $267 million as a result of higher crude oil and natural gas prices.

It realised an average $19.62 per barrel of oil, $3.11 more than a year ago and $2.66 per thousand cubic feet of natural gas, an increase of $0.51, although part was offset by a rise in exploration and production expenses $42 million.
International exploration and production earnings rose 20 percent to $156 million from $130 million, partly due to an eight percent rise in prices, but also increased production.
The international sector includes a $19 million currency gain due to the decline of sterling against the dollar.

U.S. Refining and marketing earnings continued weak in the quarter at $6.0 million compared with $4.0 million a year ago as increased refinery throughput and higher wholesale prices were offset by refinery fires in late-1996 and early 1997 and lower West Coast marketing margins.
U.S. refined product sales were just over one million barrels per day, down from 1.02 million a year ago.
In the international sector, first quarter earnings rose to $104 million from $94 million due to better results in Latin America and Europe, however Asia was weak.

International refined product sales were 1.46 million barrels per day, down from 1.65 million, as Texaco's share of production its Caltex joint venture with Chevron Corp fell to 586,000 barrels per day from 712 million.

"Caltex' improved operating margins in Korea were more than offset by unfavorable refining margins in Thailand, and higher currency losses of $26 million, mostly from the significant weakening of the Korean Won," Texaco said.
Refined product sales decreased due to Caltex' April 1, 1996, sale of its interest in refining operations in Japan and reduced purchase/sale activity to balance the system, the company said.
Capital and exploratory spending rose sharply to $799 million for the first quarter of 1997 from $641 million. ((-- David Chance New York Newsroom 212 859 1902))
